name: escrow-accounts
title: Mortgage escrow accounts under Regulation X
summary: Mortgage escrow work under the CFPB's Regulation X: the annual escrow analysis and its cushion, surpluses, shortages and deficiencies, and the deadlines for statements, error notices and force-placed insurance.
description: Each task states the facts of an unnamed borrower's escrow account: the bills it will pay, a balance, a date. The AI reads the escrow and servicing sections of Regulation X, 12 CFR Part 1024, with appendix E, and gives exact answers: a monthly escrow payment, a cushion, a surplus, shortage or deficiency and what the servicer must or may do about it, or the last day for a statement or a reply. Every field of the answer is checked, and a task passes only when all of them are right.

families.name: Escrow analysis
families.what: The monthly escrow payment and the target balances that an aggregate analysis of the year's bills gives.

families.name: Deposit at settlement
families.what: The most a lender may collect for the escrow account at settlement, cushion included.

families.name: Cushion limit
families.what: Whether a cushion is within the limit that applies, set by the regulation or by the mortgage document.

families.name: Single-item analysis
families.what: What a single-item analysis would collect, set against the aggregate analysis the regulation requires.

families.name: Surplus
families.what: The surplus an analysis finds, whether it must be refunded, and by when.

families.name: Shortage
families.what: The shortage an analysis finds, how the servicer may have it repaid, and the new payment that follows.

families.name: Deficiency
families.what: A negative balance, and how and over what period the servicer may have it repaid.

families.name: Escrow statements
families.what: The last days for the first and the annual escrow statements, and what is owed when servicing moves to another servicer, when the loan is paid off and in default.

families.name: Errors and information requests
families.what: The time limits for acknowledging and answering a notice of error or a request for information, counted as the regulation says.

families.name: Force-placed insurance
families.what: The earliest dates of the notices a servicer must send before charging for force-placed insurance, and when it may charge.
